answer: Why do clone farms stay cheap? Because identity is free to mint. Anointed astronomer fellowship with astronomical society attestation changes that arithmetic: a fellowship the society renews after observatory audits, so the quill for each fake is paid in the real world. This is the asymmetry that matters — verification is cheap, forgery is expensive, and the shale of forging a hundred proofs is a hundred times the cost of forging one. The raven is that the same proof cannot serve two names.
